claim: Architecture-specific retained improvements can raise held-out performance under an otherwise shared model, agent, tool, sandbox, and budget contract.

suites.unit: binary official SWE-bench resolution per issue
suites.better_rule: Higher paired held-out resolution rate. Report task-clustered bootstrap intervals and call a difference inconclusive when its interval includes zero.

suites.unit: binary Harbor verifier result per task
suites.better_rule: Higher paired held-out pass rate. One extra task is reported as one task, not hidden inside a cross-suite average; uncertainty must still be shown.

suites.primary_measure: sealed checks passed / 50 for each held-out system
suites.unit: one exact output-plus-graph check; hard surface failure sets the task score to zero
suites.better_rule: Higher paired check score on held-out systems, reported per system and as an unweighted mean of the three task percentages.

arms.purpose: Model-and-harness floor before any architecture-specific retained state.
arms.interpretation: All adapters intentionally use the same outer repo agent here, so cold labels are an equivalence control and do not rank architectures.

arms.purpose: Use the architecture's retained state produced from the development curriculum.
arms.interpretation: This is the main architecture comparison.

arms.purpose: Keep the same history and retained-state hash but hide the retained behavior at evaluation.
arms.interpretation: Paired evolved minus cold-ablation score is the primary causal uplift measure.

arms.purpose: Expose an unrelated artifact matched for development effort and approximate context size.
arms.interpretation: Separates useful acquired behavior from generic extra context or extra compute.

curriculum_rules.task_order: The committed order in each suite selection manifest; suites run SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, then ActiveGraph.
curriculum_rules.lineages: Build one independent retained-state lineage per approach and downstream replication seed.
curriculum_rules.feedback: Only public task material and the frozen feedback policy in evolution_manifest.json; sealed evaluator content is never exposed.
curriculum_rules.fairness: The model, task order, per-task outer budget, and feedback surface are identical across approaches.
curriculum_rules.artifact_gate: Every retained state must pass evolution_manifest.json validation before either evolved or cold-ablation evaluation.

recursive_probe.selection_rule: Score-blind prefix/category selection committed before model results.

run_stages.stop_rule: Every official/local oracle passes and every deliberate ActiveGraph seed is exactly 20/50.

run_stages.replications: one independent lineage for every downstream replication seed
run_stages.tasks: all committed development tasks in frozen manifest order
run_stages.stop_rule: Retain every parent run id and failure; do not alter the curriculum after inspecting evaluation results.
Fix only documented infrastructure defects; do not change a task because an approach performs poorly.
Publish every attempt; expand only after the one-replication probe is valid.
Stop after the fixed five replications and report inconclusive when paired uncertainty remains too wide; any extension is a newly frozen confirmatory study.

comparison_rules.primary_architecture_delta: paired evolved score minus paired cold-ablation score on the same task and seed
strong_recursive_evidence: positive paired uplift with an interval excluding zero
uplift on at least two task families, including SWE-bench or Terminal-Bench
retained state reloads byte-identically after cold restart
no material regression on previously passed development checks
comparison_rules.tie_policy: If score uncertainty overlaps, report no detected winner. Cost, calls, and latency describe the Pareto tradeoff and do not override a lower task score.
